title: Pioneer motor-bicycle, c. 1901
reference: 1901 New-Werner layout and De Dion-engined motor-bicycles of 1900-1905 (generic, unbranded): bicycle diamond frame with dropped bottom loop, engine in the frame, belt drive
wheels: 26 x 2 in clincher tyres on light 28-spoke nickel wire wheels, spoon brake on the front tyre, rim plunger brake at the rear, belt rim and chain sprocket on the rear hub
engine: About 250 cc air-cooled upright single (70 mm bore) with finned cylinder, automatic atmospheric inlet valve cap, mechanical exhaust valve with pushrod, flywheel crankcase, surface/spray carburettor, trembler-coil and battery ignition, exhaust to a cylindrical silencer under the engine, flat leather belt to the rear belt rim, pedal cranks and chain on the other side
colours: Black enamel frame, fork and mudguards with gold pinstripe and tank bands; nickel fittings, wheels and handlebar; brass carbide lamp, carburettor and horn; brown leather saddle, tool bag and belt
weak_points: Fork is a plain straight-blade enamel tube pair with no crown lugs detail; flat leather belt and chain are thin and read faintly at catalogue scale; the tank is a compact rectangular box (about 15 cm long) because the down tube and exhaust pipe leave little room; no cylinder-head detail beyond the inlet cap and exhaust chamber; spoon brake and cables are small; no stitching on saddle or belt.
